messages.subject: Interpretation of QC Spacial Images
parts:
Hi,
I'm using aroma.affymetrix to plot QC spatial images (PlotImage) and was wondering if there is any documentation that would help further interpret the images.  As per the documentation, the plots are super helpful in determining standout regions that are banded or bubble-ish.  I'm plotting the Log2 transform mapped onto a rainbow palette.  Is it true that light colors map to regions of low intensity and vice versa? 

Any insights you may have with regard to gleaning information from the images would be helpful.

Thanks in advance.
Andy

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Interpretation of QC Spacial Images

On Tue, Oct 28, 2008 at 9:30 AM, Andy Reynolds <arey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
> I'm using aroma.affymetrix to plot QC spatial images (PlotImage) and was
> wondering if there is any documentation that would help further interpret
> the images. As per the documentation, the plots are super helpful in
> determining standout regions that are banded or bubble-ish. I'm plotting
> the Log2 transform mapped onto a rainbow palette. Is it true that light
> colors map to regions of low intensity and vice versa?

I guess you are referring to 'rainbow' in setup like this:

ae <- ArrayExplorer(rsList);
setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"));
process(ae, verbose=log);

That 'rainbow' string is actually referring to the name of an existing
functions, i.e. here rainbow(). You can set the range and order of
colors generated by such a function by doing something like:

col <- rainbow(256);
plot(seq(along=col), col=col, pch=19, cex=2);

As you see, the intensity/brightness of the rainbow() palette is *not*
linear. There are other palettes you can try, e.g. terrain.colors()
etc. See the help pages for one of them and you'll find more. The
r-help list is a good list to ask for more info on this.

BTW, in the above ArrayExplorer example (see also last figure in
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/generic-quality-assessment),
the "white" (transparent actually) dots (can also) indicate missing
values.

Hope this helps

Henrik
